narrative: Material PL1__M3FEC07A exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=0.335) with a mean of 734 units/day across 136 working days, approximating a normal distribution. Lead times average 4.08 days with moderate stability after removing two erroneous observations exceeding 9,000 days. The current SAP safety stock of 182 units is critically insufficient; a safety stock of 2,015 units is required to achieve the 95% service level target. An (r,Q) policy with reorder point 5,012 and order quantity 4,569 (storage-capped) reduces total annual cost by 36.8% versus the SAP baseline.
warnings: SAP safety stock (182) is critically low vs recommended (2015) — severe stockout risk under current policy
Order quantity capped at 4569 by max_storage_units constraint (6584.951 - 2015 = 4569)
2 extreme lead time outliers removed (9201.55, 9327.37 days) — investigate source data in ERP

research_insights.selection_rationale: With moderate CV (0.335), approximately-normal demand, and stable-to-moderate lead times, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy provides efficient service-level targeting via the z-factor safety stock formula without requiring the complexity of (s,S) or periodic-review models.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is the binding constraint on order quantity (capped at 4,569 vs unconstrained EOQ of 3,467 which was below MOQ=2,192; the binding cap comes from max_storage_units). If demand spikes or safety stock needs increase, the current storage limit will prevent adequate replenishment batch sizes, increasing stockout risk.
